functional_semantics.triton: field i decoded as ((b_uint8 & (3<<2i)) >> 2i).to(int8) - 1 paired with A columns i*K_b + j*BLOCK_K (impl_triton.py:72-77); int32 accumulation; int32 output.
functional_semantics.cutile: same decode ((B_int32 & mask) >> 2i) - 1 cast to int8, A block k_a = i*num_tiles_kb + j (impl_cutile.py:56-66); int32 accumulation; int32 output.
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py:10-19 (host unpack to rows i*K_b + r, fp32 matmul with TF32 disabled, cast to int32, exact for the generated ranges). Generator tensors.py:439-448 returns int8 A and packed uint8 B; the config dtype label is ignored.

stages.note: Single-kernel blocked GEMM with grouped ordering and in-mainloop decode on both sides.

dependencies.triton: kernel depends on c and on bt (impl_triton.py:128,132/141).
dependencies.note: No intermediates besides the Triton-side bt (see preprocessing).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: outer loop over packed tiles j, inner static loop over fields i, int32 MMA accumulation (impl_triton.py:68-77).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: same j-outer / i-inner nesting with int32 MMA (impl_cutile.py:50-66).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same non-monotone logical-K visiting order; irrelevant for exact integer accumulation.

precision.triton: int8 x int8 -> int32 via tl.dot out_dtype=int32 (impl_triton.py:63,77); no float path.
precision.cutile: int8 x int8 -> int32 via ct.mma into an int32 accumulator (impl_cutile.py:46,66).
precision.note: Exact integer arithmetic on both sides; config.verify 0.1/0.1 is effectively exact for int32 outputs.

preprocessing.triton: bt = b.t().contiguous() (N, K_b) cached in a module-level WeakTensorKeyDictionary keyed by the B tensor object (impl_triton.py:16-24), looked up on every run (128): the transpose copy executes once per live B (warmup) and is untimed thereafter.
preprocessing.cutile: packed B consumed row-major as (TK, TN) tiles directly (impl_cutile.py:51-54); no cache, no transpose.
preprocessing.note: Genuine F/Q boundary divergence (same shape as matmul_fp32_fp16_fp8, but without the stale-address hazard because the key is weak). The contract requires any repack to be per call and uncached and lists the question as open.

intermediate_storage.triton: bt (N, K_b) uint8 retained for the lifetime of each B tensor (impl_triton.py:16-24).
intermediate_storage.cutile: none; widened B tile and decoded operand tiles are register resident (impl_cutile.py:55-65).
intermediate_storage.note: Cross-call persistent operand copy vs none; same root cause as the preprocessing divergence.

mutation.triton: a, b never written; fresh c per call (impl_triton.py:127).
mutation.cutile: a, b never written; fresh c per call (impl_cutile.py:82).
mutation.note: Idempotent. The reference sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False process-wide inside run() without restoring it (impl_torch.py:17).

hardware_dispatch.triton: no dispatch branches; K is a constexpr with static_assert K % (4*BLOCK_K) == 0 (impl_triton.py:40,46-49).
hardware_dispatch.cutile: no dispatch branches; K_b is ConstInt (impl_cutile.py:29); slab index k_a = i*num_tiles_kb + j is only exact when K_b is a multiple of the K tile (57).
hardware_dispatch.note: Both sides are specialised per K and rely on tile-aligned K_b for the swept shapes (K = 1024*i); the contract records general-K support as an open question. Descriptor-based vs tile loads are mapping details.

fq_boundary.note: The formula counts A once (int8), the packed B once (K*N/4 bytes) and C once (int32), with element sizes hard-coded. The cuTile path matches it by reading the packed B directly and decoding in registers. The Triton path matches it in steady state only because the K-major copy of the packed B (read + write of K*N/4 bytes plus one copy launch) runs once per live B and is cached in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary (impl_triton.py:16-24,128), so it is never timed after warmup: the formula implicitly credits a free prepacked B on that side. A generated implementation transposing per call carries 2*K*N/4 bytes of uncounted timed traffic. The reference's host unpack and fp32 GEMM are reference-side work, not an F/Q issue.

review_items: Decide whether the K-major repack of the packed B is inside the timed algorithm: the contract requires any repack to be per call and uncached, but the manual Triton timing excludes it (bt cached in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary, impl_triton.py:16-24,128); either re-measure the Triton reference with a per-call transpose or direct (K_b, N) consumption, or mark its numbers as not comparable to contract-conforming implementations.

Decide whether the contract must require correctness for arbitrary K_b: the manual Triton kernel enforces K % (4*BLOCK_K) == 0 by static_assert (impl_triton.py:46-49) and the manual cuTile slab index k_a = i*num_tiles_kb + j (impl_cutile.py:57) is only exact when K_b is a multiple of its K tile, while a zero-padded packed byte decodes to -1; the contract currently requires correctness for the swept shapes and masking of any tail.

impl_torch.py:17 sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False process-wide inside run() and never restores it; decide whether the harness isolates this, since it changes the fp32 reference of matmul_fp32_fp16_fp8 (which sets the flag True at import) when both run in one process.
